steps.title: Open the Structure page
steps.narration: We start on the Structure page — Tapeology's map of where a stock's price tends to react. Nothing to sign into anywhere in this app.
steps.point_out: The page opens straight into a short, clean tradable map rather than a wall of raw levels — that decluttering is the foundation this chapter's new work sits on top of.

expect.text: Choose a symbol and an as-of time, then Load, to see its tradable level map.

steps.title: The edge report keeps computing quietly
steps.narration: Scrolling down to the Edge Report — the honest scorecard comparing three trading strategies over every recorded price reaction.
steps.point_out: This report used to restart its multi-hour computation from scratch on every single visit. Now, once it finishes computing one time, that answer is saved — every later visit, even after a restart, loads in seconds instead of hours. Right now it's still on that very first real run, so what's on screen is its own honest "still working, nothing faked yet" state.

expect.text: The v1 / structure_tape / structure_tape_map comparison over recorded event windows

steps.title: Enter a symbol
steps.narration: Typing AAPL into the Symbol field at the top of the page.

steps.title: Pick the pinned session
steps.narration: Typing in the as-of time for a real AAPL session that tested its own resistance zone.

steps.title: Load the tradable map
steps.narration: Clicking Load turns thousands of raw price levels into a short, ranked list of the ones that actually matter.
steps.point_out: The map resolves to a ten-row table, and the top resistance zone lands right around $300-302 — the real Apple wall — ranked Class A, exactly where it should be.

steps.title: Reveal the full raw levels, on demand
steps.narration: The clean map is the default view — clicking "Show raw levels" reveals the older, denser picture underneath, for anyone who wants it.
steps.point_out: A dense multi-timeframe level chart and a confluence-zones panel appear below — the same underlying level data as before, just tucked behind a toggle instead of leading the page.

steps.title: Search the case-study registry
steps.narration: Further down the page, every recorded price-zone touch across twelve stocks is browsable and filterable — over 800 real examples. Typing a symbol that doesn't exist proves the filter is real, not decoration.
steps.point_out: The table honestly reports no matches for this filter, with a note confirming the registry still has real rows — this combination simply matches none.

steps.title: Clear the filter
steps.narration: Clearing the field instantly brings every recorded touch back — this is just filtering data that's already loaded, no new fetch needed.

steps.title: Back to the live cockpit
steps.narration: Moving over to the cockpit — the page traders actually watch while a session is live.

steps.title: Watch a simulated ticker
steps.narration: Typing in a simulated ticker before clicking Watch.

steps.title: Simulated chart, honest empty state
steps.narration: The candlestick chart and tape-state markers appear immediately for the simulated ticker.
steps.point_out: Directly below the chart, an honest "No tradable map for SIM-BUYER." message shows instead of a fake band — simulated tickers have no real market structure to compare against, and the app says so plainly.

steps.title: Stop watching
steps.narration: Stopping the simulated watch before switching over to a real symbol.

steps.title: Switch to Live mode
steps.narration: Switching the data source over to Live.

steps.title: Type a real symbol
steps.narration: Typing AAPL into the symbol field again, this time for the live feed.

steps.title: Live mode: its own dedicated view
steps.point_out: The price chart and band overlay from Simulated and Historical modes are completely absent here — Live mode stays a pure real-time tape reader, never anything trade-related.
